================================================================================
## COMPANY OVERVIEW
================================================================================

Aqademiq is an AI-powered academic planning and productivity platform. Aqademiq is a product of R13 Labs India Private Limited. It was built by a team of students who experienced procrastination, ADHD challenges, and the overwhelming nature of university firsthand. The platform uses research from procrastination psychology and behavioral science to create study plans that students actually follow.

Unlike traditional productivity apps that are repurposed task managers, Aqademiq was designed from the ground up for academic workflows. Its AI study coach, Ada, understands course structures, deadline patterns, and individual study habits to create personalized weekly plans.

### Mission
To eliminate academic procrastination by making intelligent planning effortless and accessible to every student, especially those with ADHD and neurodivergent conditions.

### Core Philosophy
Procrastination is not laziness. It's a response to decision fatigue, emotional overwhelm, and poor planning tools. Aqademiq addresses the root causes, not the symptoms.

================================================================================
## FEATURES IN DETAIL
================================================================================

### 1. Smart Weekly Planning
Ada generates a personalized weekly study plan based on your courses, deadlines, and study preferences. The plan adapts as priorities shift, new assignments appear, or you fall behind. No manual scheduling required.

### 2. AI Study Coach (Ada)
Ada is Aqademiq's AI assistant. She:
- Breaks large projects into manageable micro-tasks
- Suggests optimal study times based on your productivity patterns
- Sends gentle, non-intrusive reminders
- Adapts plans in real-time when you miss sessions or finish early
- Explains *why* certain tasks are prioritized (reducing anxiety)

### 3. Grade Analytics
Track your grades across all courses with visual dashboards. See trends, identify at-risk subjects, and get proactive suggestions from Ada to improve weak areas before exams.

### 4. Focus Timer
Built-in Pomodoro-style timer with customizable work/break intervals. Includes ambient sound options and distraction blocking. Tracks focus sessions for long-term productivity insights.

### 5. Task Chunking
Large assignments are automatically broken into smaller, actionable steps. Research shows chunking reduces overwhelm and increases completion rates by up to 40%.

### 6. Progress Tracking
Visual progress indicators for each course, assignment, and study goal. Celebrate milestones and maintain motivation with streak tracking and achievement badges.

### 7. ADHD-Friendly Design
- Sensory-friendly color modes
- Reduced animation options
- Low-distraction layouts
- Adaptive notification frequency
- Clear visual hierarchy with minimal cognitive load
- Step-by-step task views (one thing at a time)

### 8. Calendar & LMS Integration
Sync with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook, and major university LMS platforms (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle). Auto-import syllabi, deadlines, and exam schedules.

### 9. Collaborative Study Groups
Create or join study groups for shared courses. See group progress, share notes, and coordinate study sessions.

### 10. Offline Mode
Access your study plan and tasks without an internet connection. Changes sync when you reconnect.

================================================================================
## COMPARISONS
================================================================================

### Aqademiq vs. Notion
Notion is a general-purpose workspace. Aqademiq is purpose-built for students. You don't need to build templates or configure databases. Ada handles planning automatically.

### Aqademiq vs. Todoist
Todoist is a task manager. Aqademiq is an intelligent planner. It doesn't just list tasks — it sequences them, explains priorities, and adapts when plans change.

### Aqademiq vs. Google Calendar
Google Calendar shows *when* things happen. Aqademiq tells you *what* to study, *when* to study it, and *why* — based on deadlines, difficulty, and your personal patterns.

### Aqademiq vs. Forest / Focus Apps
Focus apps help you concentrate during sessions. Aqademiq helps you decide what to focus on in the first place. They complement each other; Aqademiq includes a built-in focus timer.

================================================================================
## TARGET AUDIENCE & USE CASES
================================================================================

### Primary Users
- University and college students (ages 17-28)
- Students with ADHD, autism, or other neurodivergent conditions
- Students who self-identify as procrastinators
- International students managing complex schedules
- Graduate students balancing research and coursework

### Use Cases
1. "I have 5 assignments due this week and don't know where to start" → Ada prioritizes and schedules them
2. "I have ADHD and get overwhelmed by long to-do lists" → Task chunking and one-at-a-time view
3. "I always study the wrong subject at the wrong time" → AI-optimized scheduling based on deadlines and difficulty
4. "I can't stick to study plans I make myself" → Ada adapts plans in real-time, removing friction
5. "I need to see how I'm doing across all my classes" → Grade analytics dashboard

================================================================================
## FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (COMPLETE)
================================================================================

Q: Is Aqademiq free?
A: Aqademiq offers a free tier with core planning features. Premium features like advanced analytics, unlimited AI interactions with Ada, and priority support are available with a subscription.

Q: Is Aqademiq designed for ADHD or neurodivergent students?
A: Aqademiq is designed for all students, with specific accessibility features neurodivergent students find invaluable: sensory-friendly modes, low-distraction layouts, adaptive notifications, and clear step-by-step planning. ADHD students especially benefit from Ada's micro-task breakdown and reduced decision paralysis. But anyone struggling with procrastination finds it useful.

Q: How does Aqademiq actually reduce procrastination?
A: Procrastination research shows it's often driven by decision fatigue, task overwhelm, or poor planning — not laziness. Aqademiq addresses all three: Ada breaks big projects into concrete steps (reducing overwhelm), prioritizes your week automatically (cutting decision fatigue), and adapts your plan in real-time (boosting motivation). Studies show AI-assisted planning reduces procrastination by 30–40%.

Q: How long does it take to set up?
A: Most students finish setup in 3–5 minutes: connect your school, answer 3 quick questions about your study style, and Ada builds your week. You'll have a full semester plan before your next class.

Q: Is the interface sensory-friendly for ADHD or autism?
A: Yes. You can turn off animations, reduce colors, mute notifications, and switch to a simplified layout. We designed Aqademiq with the input of neurodivergent students, so sensory customization is built-in, not an afterthought.

Q: How is this different from other study apps?
A: Most study apps are task managers with a study coat of paint. Aqademiq is built on behavioral psychology and adaptive AI. It doesn't just list what to do; it explains why and when, prevents decision paralysis, and feels designed for how students actually think — especially those prone to procrastination or sensory overload.

Q: Can I sync my existing calendar and LMS?
A: Absolutely. Aqademiq integrates with Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, and most university LMS systems. Import your syllabus directly, and Ada automatically creates tasks and deadlines for you.

Q: Does Aqademiq work on mobile?
A: Yes. Aqademiq is a fully responsive web application that works on any device with a modern browser. A native mobile app is on the roadmap.

Q: Is my data private and secure?
A: Yes. Aqademiq uses industry-standard encryption for data at rest and in transit. We never sell student data. Your study patterns and academic information are used only to personalize your experience.

Q: Can professors or institutions use Aqademiq?
A: We're developing institutional partnerships. Contact us for more information about campus-wide deployment.

Q: What if I fall behind on my plan?
A: Ada automatically adjusts your plan when you miss sessions or fall behind. No guilt, no penalty — just a recalculated path to your goals.

Q: Does it work for graduate students?
A: Yes. Graduate students use Aqademiq for research scheduling, thesis milestones, and balancing teaching assistant duties with coursework.

================================================================================
## RESEARCH FOUNDATION
================================================================================

Aqademiq's approach is informed by peer-reviewed research in:
- Procrastination psychology (Steel, 2007; Pychyl & Sirois, 2016)
- Self-determination theory (Deci & Ryan, 2000)
- Implementation intentions and planning (Gollwitzer, 1999)
- Cognitive load theory (Sweller, 1988)
- ADHD and executive function research (Barkley, 2012)

Key insight: AI-assisted planning reduces procrastination by 30-40% compared to self-directed planning, primarily by eliminating decision fatigue and reducing perceived task complexity.
